text: Do not make idols for yourselves; do not set up a carved image or a sacred pillar, and do not place a figured stone in your land to bow down before it, for I am the LORD your God.
Keep my Sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
If you live by my statutes and keep my commandments and carry them out,
I will give you rain in its season, the land will yield its produce, and the trees of the field will give their fruit.
Your threshing will last until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest until sowing time. You will eat your bread until you are satisfied and live securely in your land.
I will grant peace in the land; you will lie down with no one to make you afraid. I will rid the land of dangerous beasts, and no sword will pass through your land.
You will pursue your enemies, and they will fall before you by the sword.
Five of you will chase a hundred, and a hundred of you will chase ten thousand; your enemies will fall before you by the sword.
I will turn toward you, make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will establish my covenant with you.

versions.text: I will turn toward you, make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will uphold my covenant with you.
versions.explanation: The verb הקימותי means to establish or confirm a covenant, an act that brings it into force; "uphold" suggests merely maintaining something already in place and weakens the promise.

text: You will still be eating last year's harvest when you must clear it out to make room for the new.
I will set my dwelling among you, and I will not reject you.
I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be my people.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt so that you would no longer be their slaves. I broke the bars of your yoke and made you walk upright.
But if you will not listen to me and will not carry out all these commandments,
if you reject my statutes and despise my ordinances, refusing to keep all my commandments and breaking my covenant,
then I in turn will do this to you: I will bring terror upon you—wasting disease and fever that destroy the eyes and drain away life. You will sow your seed in vain, for your enemies will eat it.
I will set my face against you, and you will be struck down before your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee when no one is chasing you.
If after all this you still will not listen to me, I will go on to discipline you seven times over for your sins.
I will break your stubborn pride. I will make your sky like iron and your land like bronze.
Your strength will be spent for nothing, for your land will not yield its produce, and the trees of the land will not give their fruit.
If you continue to defy me and refuse to listen to me, I will multiply your afflictions seven times over, as your sins deserve.
I will send wild animals against you; they will rob you of your children, destroy your livestock, and reduce your numbers, and your roads will lie deserted.

versions.text: I will send wild animals against you; they will rob you of your children, destroy your livestock, and reduce your numbers until your roads lie deserted.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew lists the desolation of the roads as a further consequence joined by "and," not as a temporal limit ("until"), which introduces a nuance not in the text.

text: If even then you are not corrected by me but continue to defy me,
then I too will walk in hostility against you, and I myself will strike you seven times over for your sins.

versions.text: then I too will defy you, and I myself will strike you seven times over for your sins.
versions.explanation: Describing God as "defying" his people is theologically awkward, since defiance implies resistance to a superior; the Hebrew idiom הלך בקרי means to act with hostility or opposition, which is better rendered for God's side of the clause.

text: I will bring the sword against you to avenge the covenant. When you withdraw into your cities, I will send a plague among you, and you will be handed over to the enemy.
When I cut off your supply of bread, ten women will bake your bread in a single oven and dole it out to you by weight; you will eat and not be satisfied.
If after all this you still will not listen to me but continue to defy me,
then in furious defiance I will oppose you, and I myself will discipline you seven times over for your sins.
You will eat the flesh of your sons; the flesh of your daughters you will eat.
I will destroy your high places, cut down your incense altars, and pile your corpses on the lifeless forms of your idols; and I will reject you.
I will turn your cities into ruins and lay waste your sanctuaries, and I will take no delight in the pleasing aroma of your offerings.
I myself will lay the land waste, so that your enemies who settle in it will be appalled at it.
I will scatter you among the nations and unsheathe the sword after you. Your land will become a wasteland and your cities a ruin.
Then the land will enjoy its sabbaths all the days it lies desolate while you are in the land of your enemies; then the land will rest and enjoy its sabbaths.
All the days of its desolation it will have the rest it did not have during your sabbaths when you lived on it.

As for those of you who survive, I will fill their hearts with dread in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a windblown leaf will send them running; they will flee as though from the sword and fall when no one is chasing them.
They will stumble over one another as if fleeing the sword, though no one pursues. You will have no power to stand before your enemies.
You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will devour you.
Those of you who are left will waste away in the lands of your enemies because of their guilt; they will waste away because of their fathers' guilt as well.
But if they confess their guilt and the guilt of their fathers—their treachery against me and their defiance of me,
I too walked against them in hostility and brought them into the land of their enemies—if then their uncircumcised hearts are humbled and they make amends for their guilt,

versions.text: which made me oppose them and bring them into the land of their enemies—if then their uncircumcised hearts are humbled and they make amends for their guilt,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew opens with the emphatic "I also/I too" (אַף־אֲנִי) and states God's own action as a parallel response to Israel's hostility; rendering it as a relative clause ("which made me") turns God's declaration into a consequence caused by Israel and loses the deliberate mirroring of "walking in hostility" from the earlier verses.

versions.text: then I too walked against them in hostility and brought them into the land of their enemies—if then their uncircumcised hearts are humbled and they make amends for their guilt,
versions.explanation: The opening "then" signals an apodosis, but grammatically this clause is still part of the long conditional begun in v. 40; the real "then" comes with "I will remember my covenant" in v. 42. Dropping the initial "then" preserves the emphatic "I too" (אַף־אֲנִי) without prematurely closing the conditional, and it also removes the awkward doubling of "then ... if then" for the ear.

text: I will remember my covenant with Jacob, and my covenant with Isaac, and my covenant with Abraham I will remember; and I will remember the land.

But the land will be left empty by them and will enjoy its sabbaths while it lies desolate without them, and they will make amends for their guilt, because they rejected my ordinances and their soul despised my statutes.

versions.text: For the land will be abandoned by them and will enjoy its sabbaths while it lies desolate without them, and they will make amends for their guilt, because they rejected my ordinances and despised my statutes.
versions.explanation: The waw here marks a contrast/continuation, not a causal "For"; "But" reads more naturally in oral delivery. Also, the Hebrew emphasizes that it was "their soul" that abhorred the statutes (גָּעֲלָה נַפְשָׁם), which strengthens the parallel with "they rejected."

text: Yet even then, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or despise them so as to destroy them completely and break my covenant with them, for I am the LORD their God.
For their sake I will remember the covenant with their ancestors, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, to be their God. I am the LORD.
These are the statutes, ordinances, and instructions that the LORD established between himself and the Israelites on Mount Sinai through Moses.
